choices.english: Israel gave up being ruled by God as their king through the prophets
choices.why: ἀποφοιτάω 'give up, cease from'; βασιλεύεσθαι is passive, 'to be ruled as by a king'.

pass_a_gloss: [Of Cyril.] Departed from (ἀποφοιτάω) Israel the being ruled as king (βασιλεύομαι) by God through prophets; called for king a man. Thereby also slipped from (ἀπολισθαίνω) the commandment (ἐντολή): first for Solomon worshipped (προσκυνέω) the Baals (Βααλείμ); then after him Jeroboam the heifers (δάμαλις) set up (ἀνίστημι). Lemma: And said Lord to Samuel: Hear the voice of them, etc. [Of Cyril.] Having well the affairs for them, and in order the best lying, bitter things against themselves the wretched (δείλαιοι) planned (φρονέω). Shaking off (ἀποσείομαι) as it were of the under God kingdom (βασιλεία) the yoke (ζυγός), they came saying to the blessed Samuel: Appoint over us king to judge (δικάζω) us, and the rest. Then the blessed Samuel the rights (δικαιώματα) of the king announcing (καταγγέλλω) to them, and with many very terrors (δεῖμα) frightening (καταπτοέω), and turning away (ἀφίστημι) very vigorously (γοργῶς) [sentence continues in b01-rem mid].
pass_b_english: Israel gave up being ruled by God as their king through the prophets, and called for a man as king. For this very reason they also slipped from the commandment: for Solomon was the first to worship the Baals (1 Kings 11:5–8), and then after him Jeroboam set up the heifers (1 Kings 12:28–29).

“And the Lord said to Samuel, ‘Listen to their voice,’” and so on (1 Samuel 8:22). Though their affairs were going well for them and were set in the best of order, the wretched people planned bitter things against themselves. Shaking off, as it were, the yoke of the kingdom under God, they came to the blessed Samuel, saying: “Appoint a king over us to judge us” (1 Samuel 8:5), and the rest. Then, when the blessed Samuel announced to them the rights of the king (1 Samuel 8:11–18), filling them with many terrors, and very earnestly trying to turn them away…
source_text:
{Κυρίλλου.} Ἀπεφοίτησε μὲν ὁ Ἰσραὴλ τοῦ βασιλεύεσθαι παρὰ Θεοῦ διὰ προφητῶν·
ἐκαλέσατο δὲ βασιλέα ἄνθρωπον. Ταύτῃ τοι καὶ ἀπώλισθε τῆς 69.681 ἐντολῆς·
πρῶτος γὰρ Σολομὼν προσεκύνησε τοῖς Βααλείμ· εἶτα μετ' αὐτὸν Ἱεροβοὰμ τὰς
δαμάλεις ἀνέστησεν. Καὶ εἶπεν Κύριος πρὸς Σαμουήλ· Ἄκουε τῆς φωνῆς αὐτῶν,
κ.τ.λ. {Κυρίλλου.} Ἐχόντων εὖ τῶν πραγμάτων αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐν τάξει τῇ παναρίστῃ
κειμένων, πικρὰ καθ' ἑαυτῶν οἱ δείλαιοι πεφρονήκασιν. Ἀποσειόμενοι δὲ ὥσπερ τῆς
ὑπὸ Θεῷ βασιλείας τὸν ζυγὸν, προσῄεσαν λέγοντες τῷ μακαρίῳ Σαμουήλ·
Κατάστησον ἐφ' ἡμᾶς βασιλέα δικάζειν ἡμᾶς, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς·
Εἶτα τοῦ μακαρίου Σαμουὴλ τὰ δικαιώματα τοῦ βασιλέως καταγγέλλοντος
αὐτοῖς, καὶ πολλοῖς ἄγαν καταπτοοῦντος δείμασιν, ἀφιστάντος δὲ καὶ μάλα γοργῶς

review_notes: Catena sigla '{Κυρίλλου.}' (of Cyril) are not rendered in the reading text; the first comment answers the lemma 1 Samuel 8:5 at the end of the previous section.
The column number 69.681 inside the text is not rendered.
'δαμάλεις' rendered 'heifers', as in the LXX of 3 Kingdoms 12:28; English Bibles say 'calves'.
The last sentence breaks off mid-clause at the section boundary and continues in the next section; marked with an ellipsis.

Every clause of the English was read against the PG 69 Greek of this section on 2026-10-23: no omission or addition found; negation, agency, modality and the Scripture citations were checked (LXX Kingdoms and Psalm numbers converted to English Bible numbering).
